a biomimetic tendon-based artificial finger actuation system, with one-way shape memory alloys as the actuation mechanism, is feasible and effective.

a biomimetic actuation system based on compliant tendon cables and SMA wires can be successfully implemented in a tendon-driven finger actuation system, and that a combination of microcontroller-based PD and jerk-based trajectory feedforward control can provide a high degree of naturalness in the joint motions of a 4 DOF biomimetic finger system.

the development of an SMA-based tendon-driven actuator system and a biomimetic robotic finger for the purpose of emulating natural finger joint motions.
the development and evaluation of a novel biomimetic tendon-based actuation system for artificial fingers, and the development of a control system for the actuation system.
the development of an SMA-based actuation system for artificial fingers and the design of a control system for the biomimetic actuator.

the proposed biomimetic SMA-based actuation system has the potential of being a good candidate for the design of prosthetic and wearable robotics hands.

the proposed actuation and finger systems are capable of providing a high level of biomimetic performance in terms of both kinematics and dynamics, and are suitable for prosthetic and robotic hand applications.

the proposed biomimetic tendon-actuated finger system has demonstrated its capability to emulate the natural human finger motions, and it is a good platform to develop more advanced controllers for prosthetic and rehabilitation applications.

a biomimetic SMA-based actuation system can be designed and implemented for a biomimetic finger system to achieve natural finger motions with high accuracy and repeatability.
the design and control of tendon-driven SMA actuation systems are feasible and can be applied for biomimetic prosthetic and robotic hand systems.

the biomimetic design of the tendon-driven actuation systems and the proposed control strategy can significantly improve the performance of artificial fingers, especially in terms of their dynamic response, and thus their overall dexterity.

the proposed biomimetic tendon-based actuation system can provide a simple, low-cost, and lightweight solution for the design of biomimetic prosthetic hands, as well as the development of wearable robotic hands for human–robot collaboration and teleoperation applications.
